alignments.note: Waw rendered But, which is on rule 14's open list.
Construct noun with a supplied the, no article morpheme present (rule 29).
Anarthrous substantival adjective takes the supplied the (rule 46) with the chain's of (rule 19).
Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula (rule 49), headed on the preposition's own word.
The ASV renders the rectum attributively (rule 28), so the construct noun is the English head and takes the single supplied determiner (rule 29); the unit is discontinuous around dawning (rule 25).
Nomen rectum rendered attributively as dawning (rule 28).

The participle of progression is what the ASV writes as more and more (rule 56's auxiliary-verb clause), and as the first of the coordinated attributives it takes the single supplied relative (rule 41), the unit discontinuous around shineth (rule 25). The and inside more and more coordinates the parts of this one rendering rather than two source items (rule 14). The competing reading gives That to the second participle, whose word it stands beside.
The clause's one and stands inside more and more, which is a single morpheme's rendering, so no connective is written for this waw (rule 14).
Participle rendered by the finite shineth.
Article on the rectum takes the written the before a supplied one does (rules 29, 47).

review_notes: more and more is read as the progression participle's own rendering under rule 56, with the coordinating and inside it (rule 14) and the waw consequently unrepresented; the alternative gives the and to the waw and leaves the participle only more.
The supplied relative That is given to the first of the two coordinated attributive participles (rule 41); the competing reading attaches it to shineth, and is named here under rule 8.
